slides.title: Brussels eyes a €50bn equity fund
body: The European Commission, the EU's executive arm, has **proposed a €50bn fund**. It would take direct stakes in European AI and quantum computing companies, The Next Web reports.

slides.title: Less reliance on US and China
body: The Sovereign Tech Equity Fund was confirmed on Wednesday, hours after the Financial Times first reported it, citing two officials. Its goal: cut the bloc's dependence on **US and Chinese technology**.

slides.title: It sits inside the Quantum Act
body: The legal basis sits in the **Quantum Act**, which the Commission presented the same day in Strasbourg. Henna Virkkunen, the Commission's tech chief, said the fund would reach beyond quantum to all technologies the EU deems critical.

slides.title: Europe gets only 5% of venture capital
body: "No company should be obliged to leave Europe due to lack of finance," Virkkunen told reporters. Europe attracts only around **5% of global venture capital**, according to the FT's report.

slides.title: A smaller EU fund exists
body: The €5bn Scaleup Europe Fund, managed by private equity firm EQT, made its first investments this autumn, starting with Finnish satellite firm ICEYE. The Commission hopes to grow it to **€25bn**.

facts.text: The European Commission has proposed a €50bn fund that would take direct stakes in European AI and quantum computing companies.
The Sovereign Tech Equity Fund was confirmed on Wednesday, hours after the Financial Times first reported the plan, citing two officials.
Its goal is to cut the bloc's dependence on US and Chinese technology.
The legal basis for the fund sits inside the Quantum Act, which the Commission presented the same day in Strasbourg.
Henna Virkkunen, the Commission's tech chief, said the vehicle would reach beyond quantum to all technologies the EU deems critical.
"No company should be obliged to leave Europe due to lack of finance," Virkkunen told reporters.
Europe attracts only around 5% of global venture capital flows, according to the FT's report.

Existing schemes: the €5bn Scaleup Europe Fund, managed by private equity firm EQT, made its first investments this autumn, starting with Finnish satellite firm ICEYE; the Commission hopes to grow it to €25bn.

caption:
The European Commission has proposed a €50bn fund to take direct stakes in European AI and quantum companies.

The Next Web reports the plan, first reported by the Financial Times, aims to cut the EU's dependence on US and Chinese technology. It is a proposal, not an approved fund.

→ The fund would take direct stakes in European AI and quantum computing firms
→ Tech chief Henna Virkkunen said it would reach all technologies the EU deems critical
→ Europe attracts only about 5% of global venture capital, per the FT's report
